strategy.angle: The shift toward sovereign AI infrastructure and domestic supply chains.
strategy.audience: Houston business leaders, C-suite executives, and operations directors.

draft.hook: The era of cheap, globalized AI hardware is effectively over—and Houston’s enterprise sector is about to feel the ripple effect.
draft.body:
OpenAI’s partnership with Foxconn to onshore advanced data-center hardware components isn't just a manufacturing pivot; it is the birth of 'sovereign AI' infrastructure. For Houston companies, this means your tech stack is moving from a globalized convenience to a national security asset. When we talk about AI at Amplify Intelligence, we are no longer just looking at software models; we are analyzing the physical supply chain bottlenecks that could stall your digitization efforts for years.

Why this shift now? The answer is simple: risk mitigation. With 70% of high-end semiconductor assembly currently concentrated in high-geopolitical-risk zones, companies reliance on offshore hardware is becoming a liability rather than a cost-saving strategy. 

How should Houston’s leadership respond? Stop viewing hardware procurement as an IT line item and start treating it as a strategic supply chain pillar. If you aren't auditing your vendor's hardware origins today, you’re pricing in a catastrophic failure tomorrow.
